text:
Claire: Heads up — we're seeing incomplete traces for kv-store requests, lots of spans missing after the gateway.
Ajay: Which traces? got an example?
Claire: https://traces.redwood.local/trace/abcd1234 — shows root + DB spans but no shard spans after gateway handoff.
matt: I saw similar after exporter restart earlier. exporter logs showed backpressure and dropped batches.
infra-bot: exporter-service restarted at 2025-05-12T09:03:21Z by deploy pipeline (build: ci-2025-05-12-09).
Ajay: Can you paste the gateway headers for a request? Are we propagating traceparent/tracestate?
Claire: Payload sample captured from the client: 
`traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`
`tracestate: vendor1=abc`
But kv-shard service logs show incoming request without trace headers.
matt: I think we had a change in the retry middleware last week that mutates headers. Could be stripping hop-by-hop or copying a blank headers object in some paths.
Ajay: What OpenTelemetry versions are running? we had an upgrade last week right?
Claire: gateway: otel-js 1.20.0, kv-shard: otel-js 1.18.3.
matt: 1.20 had a context propagation tweak — but that affects SDK context keys, not raw HTTP headers. Still, mismatch could surface as instrumentation differences.
Ajay: Another theory: exporter outage caused buffers to fill and our sampler/export path returned errors, triggering logic that drops spans early, then downstream services started fresh traces without parent. Any exporter logs?
Claire: exporter logs show:
`WARN otlp_exporter.py: buffering limit reached, dropping 120 spans`
`ERROR otlp_exporter.py: failed to flush batch to collector: HTTP 503`
matt: confirmed buffer overflow on the exporter. But buffer overflow alone doesn't explain missing trace headers on the HTTP handoff unless retry code lost them.
Ajay: Can you grep the gateway repo for header copies in retry code? look for `Object.assign` or direct reassign of `req.headers`.
Claire: Found snippet in gateway retry middleware: 
```
// retry middleware
req.headers = Object.assign({}, req.headers, opts.headers)
delete req.headers['x-custom-debug']
```
matt: That's the suspicious bit — if `opts.headers` is undefined in a retry path, `Object.assign` will be fine, but if `req.headers` is undefined (some code earlier replaced it) we might end up overwriting with `{}`. Also some runtime branch sets `req.headers = undefined` when normalizing.
Ajay: So the bug flow: exporter outage -> gateway experiences backpressure -> retry path kicks in -> retry middleware reassigns headers incorrectly -> trace headers dropped -> downstream services start new traces. Makes sense.
Claire: I'll patch to preserve headers: `req.headers = Object.assign({}, req.headers || {}, opts.headers || {})` and avoid deleting unknown keys. Pushing a fix to gateway: `gateway:fix/retry-preserve-headers`.
infra-bot: Rolling update started for gateway by Claire — rollout id r-20250512-01. Health checks on.
matt: We should also add unit test that simulates `opts.headers` undefined and asserts `traceparent` survives retry. I'll open a PR for tests.
Ajay: Also add a runtime metric: `ingress.traceparent_missing_total{service="gateway"}` when a request arrives with no traceparent, so we can alert early.
Claire: Agree. I'm adding the metric and will add an alert threshold at 0.1% over 5m.
product-bot: tagging @sarah-product about a retention increase request — can we retain kv-op traces 30d to help debugging for the next 48h?
Claire: Not necessary for the immediate fix, but if product signs off we can increase retention temporarily.
matt: After patch I can run a synthetic load that previously reproduced it and will post a new trace id.
Claire: Thanks — patch out in canary now. Monitoring for missing spans and `traceparent_missing_total`.
Ajay: Follow-up action items: 1) patch gateway (Claire) 2) add test (matt) 3) metric + alert (Claire) 4) review otel version skew across services (team)
Claire: On it. Thanks all :thumbsup:
